mappings.note: Accepts the late-18th-century introduction of paper currency in India but rejects exhausted metal reserves as the reason. Reasoning about why money changed form, so the economics goal.
Rejects 1947 as the date of the rupee symbol's design. A fact about the national currency under the goal.
Names the obverse of a coin. General money vocabulary under the goal.
Defines fiat money as currency whose value rests on state backing rather than material worth. Economic concept under the goal.
Which side of a note carries the heritage motifs. A fact about modern currency design under the goal.
The ox-for-several-goods example illustrating indivisibility in barter. Economic reasoning under the goal.
Contrasts the data in a QR code with the symbols punched on ancient coins - a modern payment technology (CG-SST4) set against an ancient coinage read as evidence (CG-SST2).
Matches early money forms to the regions that used them. Examples of commodity money under the economics goal rather than Indian historical coinage.
A three-way mismatch of wants resolved by money as a medium of exchange. Economic reasoning under the goal.
Sorts the qualities of good money from a non-quality. Economic reasoning under the goal.
Names the designer of the rupee symbol adopted in 2010. A fact about the national currency under the goal.
Analyses the move from barter to money and why money was necessary for economic growth. The chapter's central economic argument.
Commodity money against metallic coinage and the advantages of coins. Economic comparison under the goal; the item treats coinage generically rather than as Indian historical evidence.
Keynes on money linking present and future, worked through the store-of-value and deferred-payment functions. Economic concepts under the goal.
Asks how the metals, symbols and rulers' marks on ancient coins serve historians. Explicitly about coins as a type of historical source, which is the history goal's clause.
Weighs paper currency against metal coin. Economic reasoning about the form of money.
The RBI's role in managing the currency system. The role of a government institution in the economy, which the goal names.
Cash against UPI, cards and QR payments in today's economy. Market practice under the goal; not LO-229, because no field visit is involved.
The evolution of money as a mirror of technological and social change. A judgement about an economic institution over time, so the goal.
Names money's function as a measure of value. Economic concept under the goal.
Names the standard-of-deferred-payment function. Economic concept under the goal.
The punch-marked coins issued by early rulers as the first metallic money. Ancient Indian coinage, so the history goal.
Names minting. General money vocabulary under the goal.
Names alloy as a metal mixture used for coins. Technical vocabulary under the goal.
The names borne by ancient Indian coins. Historical coinage, so CG-SST2.
'Panam' and 'hana' as southern words for money, descended from the ancient pana. A linguistic trace of historical coinage, so CG-SST2.
Names the obverse. General coin vocabulary under the goal, as with its MCQ twin.
China as the first user of paper money. Part of the evolution of money, so the goal.
Names 'currency' for a country's coins and notes. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
The RBI as the issuing authority. A government institution in the economy, so the goal.
Names digital money. Modern payment forms under the goal.
Expands 'QR code'. Modern payment practice under the goal.
Names a non-cash payment method. Modern market practice under the goal.
Names the Junbeel Mela as the fair where barter survives. Economic institution under the goal.
Explains barter with an example. The chapter's founding concept under the goal.
The double coincidence of wants and why it limits trade. Economic reasoning under the goal.
A duplicate of the double-coincidence question with its answer appended. Same economic content, so the same code.
Carrying an ox against carrying notes - portability compared across forms of money. Economic reasoning under the goal.
Names 'rupas' as the symbols punched on ancient coins. Historical coinage read as evidence, so CG-SST2.
The Keynes quote resolved to money as a store of value. A function of money under the goal.
